newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine bourse members approve key reforms.
newsitem.headline: Philippine bourse members approve key reforms.

text.p: Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) members voted on Wednesday in favour of key reforms aimed at making the market more transparent and seat-holders more accountable, bourse officials said.
The vote clears the way for the government to grant the PSE the status of a "self-regulatory organisation" (SRO) and also helps it avoid a showdown with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The SEC had threatened to impose the changes on the PSE if its members did not accept them voluntarily.

Bourse chairman Wilson Sy welcomed the vote, saying in a statement that gaining SRO status would place the Philippines "on a par with the stock exchanges of more advanced economies, notably Tokyo in Japan and Hong Kong".
Members voted in favour of three propositions: one admitting two non-brokers to the PSE board of directors and the second providing for an annual audit of members' accounts.
The third, and most contentious, allows the PSE's surveillance department to examine members' accounts without first clearing this with the board.
One broker, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters some members had tried to postpone the vote on this third resolution but were over-ruled.
Several members were afraid the surveillance department would use its new powers in a dictatorial manner, the broker said.

"Having two outside directors will remove that clubby-clubby image. It will open the exchange and give it more transparency," Don Calderon, president of All-Asia Management Securities, told reporters.
"This will give the country a world-class exchange," Calderon said.
Sy said having non-brokers on the PSE board would greatly enhance its credibility in the eyes of both local and foreign investors.
"Such confidence in the PSE among investors will redound to a stronger Philippine capital market," Sy said.
"We want to show the world we want transparency, we want changes, we want reforms," he added.
SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay had earlier threatened to impose the new regulations on the bourse if members did not voluntarily accept the idea of policing their own ranks.
Of 186 PSE members, 152 took part in the voting, with 128 endorsing outside directors, 115 the annual audit and 110 the surveillance department examinations without board approval.
The resolution made it clear that the surveillance department would still need the approval of the PSE president, currently the only non-broker on the 15-member board.
